title: Oklahoma counts in 2018-2025 fall below a bound for rate-state populations with fixed nonnegative loading since 2017
abstract: We test whether fixed nonnegative loading after 2016 can explain the fall of Oklahoma earthquake counts. For any positive mixture of constant-normal-stress rate-state populations with fixed nonnegative loading and fixed weights, time times total mean rate cannot decrease. This gives a sharp count bound without ETAS event labels. With a 2017 origin, the mean count in 2021-2025 must be at least 0.584619 times that in 2018-2020. OGS M3+ gives 299 early and 92 late events; ComCat gives 267 and 93. If counts equal means, at least 47% and 40% of early activity lies outside this class. Independent-Poisson tests show a deficit, but 1-degree block bootstrap ranges include zero at M3+. The late period alone meets the bound. A constructed case with falling positive loading violates it without unloading. Thus heterogeneity under fixed loading cannot explain the mean pattern by itself, but the evidence does not identify the residual driver or prove negative stress. We provide the proof, checks, all count comparisons and reproducible code.
